subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm reviewing the renders for issues with the blunderbuss positioning—it seems to float away from the hand rather than being gripped naturally, and its angle looks off in both the front and three-quarter views.

Looking at the side view, the legs appear too crouched with an awkward knee bend; straightening the proportions slightly by adjusting the segment lengths would reduce the exaggerated bend while keeping the reach consistent. The knee guard spheres also seem misplaced, sitting higher up the shin near the knee rather than closer to the boots where they'd read more naturally.

Checking the pack and canteen placement, they seem to touch the torso correctly in theory but visually leave a slight gap in the side view, making the pack look like it's floating rather than resting against the back. The beard, nose, and other dwarf features read fine and appropriately exaggerated, while in the back view I'm noting a brown shape near the head that's likely the butt of the gun strapped to the back.

The gun stock poking up behind the shoulder works. For the eyes, they're small and mostly obscured by helmet brim and moustache, so I'm considering enlarging the eye decal slightly to improve readability, and brightening the pale sclera. The snow-covered base rocks look too harsh with dark undersides from the shading threshold, so lightening the rock colors would help.

The base itself feels oversized relative to the subject — currently scaled wide enough that it dominates the frame, so I'm thinking of shrinking the base radius and z-scale a bit while keeping the props (signpost, crate, keg) and rocks in roughly their relative positions.

Checking the gun/arm pose, it reads fine with the hand reaching the grip. But I'm noticing the tabard plane behind the hips sits about 5cm away from the pelvis box, floating unnaturally in side view even though it looks okay from the back — I should pull it closer to z -0.14 to close that gap.

The front tabard panel also seems to float in front of the belly, though in the three-quarter view it hangs naturally in front of the legs as if attached to the belt, so that's probably fine. I'll adjust the back tabard to roughly z -0.145 with a slight tilt, and note the left arm hangs with an open hand, wrist near the hip area.

The sleeve bands and helmet spike look fine, as do the goggles. The powder horn sticks out too far like a blade — I'll shorten its curve so it ends closer to the body. There's also a degenerate zero-radius sphere used for a glow hack that should just be removed since it's harmless but pointless. The beard braids and moustache covering the mouth both look acceptable for the dwarf design.

Checking the knee bend and boot rotation on the leg, things seem fine there too. I'm planning edits: adjust leg lengths, eye size, tabard back, remove the degenerate glow sphere, lighten the rocks, shorten the horn, and maybe tone down the nose highlight. I'm also verifying eyebrow placement doesn't overlap the eyes and double-checking leg segment lengths against the hip-to-ankle distance.

Now I'm lightening the rock mottle palette and adjusting the snow paint threshold based on surface normal, since the undersides were coming out too dark from the tone shading. Writing out the exact search-and-replace edits for the leg points array and the shell glow code...

Replacing both the stick and glow lines with a simpler block, swapping in `void shell;` to avoid an unused variable error, bumping up the eye decal size slightly, and adjusting the tabard back's position coordinates.
